sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Challenges
sections.description: This section guides the learner through the patient's initial presentation following a dog bite, focusing on the evolution from localized infection to fulminant sepsis, DIC, and multiorgan failure. It details the initial laboratory findings of pancytopenia and AKI, emphasizing the difficulty in distinguishing between pure sepsis/DIC and emerging Thrombotic Microangiopathy (TMA) in the acute phase.
subtopics: Epidemiology and transmission of Capnocytophaga canimorsus (dog bite mechanism)
Clinical timeline: From bite to septic shock and limb ischemia
Interpretation of early lab values: Sepsis vs. Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) vs. Leukemia
Differentiating Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) from early TMA
Initial management failures: Why supportive care alone was insufficient

sections.description: Focusing on the diagnostic pivot point where the patient's condition deteriorated after initial stabilization, this section teaches how to recognize secondary TMA masked by sepsis. It covers the stepwise exclusion of mimics such as Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) and Shiga-toxin HUS, utilizing specific biomarkers like ADAMTS13 activity and stool PCR.
subtopics: Recognizing Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia (MAHA): Schistocytes, rising LDH, falling haptoglobin
The role of ADAMTS13 activity in excluding TTP (PLASMIC score application)
Ruling out STEC-HUS via negative Shiga toxin PCR
Addressing confounding factors: False-positive Coombs test due to penicillin exposure
Indications for renal biopsy in adult TMA workups

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Complement-Mediated HUS and Infectious Triggers
sections.description: This section provides a focused mechanistic explanation of how C. canimorsus infection triggered Complement-Mediated HUS (CM-HUS). It contrasts hereditary forms with infection-triggered cases, explaining why genetic testing might be negative despite severe disease, and discusses the dual role of complement in fighting encapsulated bacteria versus causing endothelial damage.
subtopics: Mechanism of Alternative Pathway Dysregulation leading to endothelial injury
The 'Second Hit' theory: How C. canimorsus acts as a trigger in susceptible hosts
Genetic landscape: Distinguishing between pathogenic variants and sporadic infection-triggered cases
Why serum C3/C4 levels may appear normal during acute CM-HUS episodes
Comparison with other infectious triggers of HUS

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Strategy: Balancing Infection Control and Complement Blockade
sections.description: This section explores the complex clinical decision-making required when treating CM-HUS in the setting of active or recent bacteremia. It compares Plasma Exchange (PEX) with Eculizumab therapy, detailing the rationale for sequencing treatments, managing vaccine requirements, and mitigating infection risks associated with terminal complement inhibition.
